summary: The craft detector ran and produced 10KB of findings, and the wrapper reported 'nothing was scanned - install the detector' on a machine that already had it. ui-craft-gate.py read the subprocess output with text=True and no encoding, so a Windows console decoded it as cp1252 and the first curly quote raised UnicodeDecodeError inside the reader thread, leaving stdout empty. The empty-output guard then fired correctly for the wrong reason.
tests: ui-craft-gate.py site --markdown observed reporting nothing-scanned, then reporting 21 findings after the fix
control: encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' pinned on the subprocess.run call, with the reason and the observation recorded inline so it is not re-simplified away
boundary: Applies wherever a pack script shells out and parses text output; the encoding is part of the contract, not the locale's business. Does not apply to binary pipes.

summary: The API extractor reported 508 public symbols and members=0 for all 17 namespaces, while claiming 90.7 percent documented. A type frame was pushed with the depth at its DECLARATION line, and this codebase puts the opening brace on the NEXT line, so the pop condition depth <= recorded fired immediately and closed the type before its body began. Every member was missed and the run still reported success with a confident coverage percentage.
tests: tools/api-reference.py --json observed reporting members=0 across every namespace, then 1,711 symbols at 64.1 percent after the fix
control: An 'entered' flag on each type frame: the pop requires depth to have risen above the declaration depth first. The reason is recorded inline at the push site.
boundary: Applies to any brace-depth lexer where the opening brace may be on a later line than the declaration. Does not apply to parsers with a real syntax tree.

summary: A second episode-open on the coordination contract forked a session into two simultaneously-active Work Episodes. WorkEpisodeService.Open does not close the previous episode - it records a new one with the next generation and returns - so both rows kept ClosedAt null, both reported Active, generations climbed, and a reader would pick one without knowing the other existed. Found by a second session reading the service rather than the caller.
tests: AiDe.Core.Tests.Watcher.ContractEpisodeTests.ASecondOpen_SupersedesTheFirst_ItDoesNotForkIntoTwoActiveEpisodes - observed failing with Open, passing with Reframe
control: The ingest routes a second open through Reframe, where 'changing the goal starts a new episode' is already defined, so the rule is not re-decided at the caller. The test asserts exactly one Active and one Closed/Superseded, so removing the branch fails instead of forking.
boundary: Applies wherever a caller infers a state transition a service does not actually perform. Does not apply where the service documents the transition on the method being called.

summary: The public site's counted figures went stale three times in one session - once when a rebase raised the App test floor, again when another session's audit entries arrived, and again with five of nine wrong at once. Each hand correction was itself stale within the turn. The craft review had already recorded it as an open gap while the figures were still hand-maintained.
tests: tools/verify-site-figures.py observed reporting all five stale figures with both values before any fix, then clean after --update
control: Every figure carries data-figure=<name>; verify-site-figures.py computes each from its source of record and the Pages workflow runs it without --update so a stale page fails the build. Two DC-016 guards: it fails when no data-figure element exists at all, and on a name it cannot compute rather than skipping it.
boundary: Applies to any published literal quantity whose source keeps changing. Does not apply to a figure that is definitionally fixed, such as the six Weave dimensions.

summary: TerminalSurface.EnvironmentFor was assigned only inside AttachWorkspace, and both MainWindow call sites skip that method when the view model returns no queries. Every run that never attached a workspace launched every terminal with an empty environment - no AIDE_SESSION and no AIDE_CONTRACT_LOG - so registration still happened and the agent appeared in the watcher while being unable to write a model update or an episode. Observed and could not participate.
tests: AiDe.App.Tests.EnvironmentContractSurvivesNoWorkspaceTests - both tests observed failing with the constructor assignment removed, passing with it
control: The assignment moved to the WorkbenchShell constructor where nothing gates it; a second test asserts the unknowable variables stay ABSENT rather than taking ResolveGitFacts's fallback, so always-present cannot become always-lying.
boundary: Applies to any long-lived hook or registration assigned inside a conditional setup method when the assigned thing does not depend on that setup. Does not apply where the hook genuinely needs the setup's state to exist.

summary: CoordContractWriter used the external session id verbatim as a file name. Agent panes are agent:<name>#<hex>, and on Windows Path.Combine(dir, 'agent:claude#fb96e3.jsonl') creates the file 'agent' with an NTFS alternate data stream - the write succeeds, the bytes are there, and Directory.EnumerateFiles(dir, '*.jsonl') cannot see them. No agent session was ever registered: no liveness, no harness/model update, no episode-open. Found on the owner's machine as a zero-byte file named 'agent' holding seven streams and 41 KB of events beside terminal-1.jsonl as a real 442 KB file.
tests: AiDe.Core.Tests.Watcher.CoordLogSurvivesASessionIdWithAColonTests - 4 of 6 observed failing on the shipped shape, asserting through EnumerateFiles rather than by reading the path back
control: FileNameFor maps a session id to a safe name with a digest of the ORIGINAL id appended, so two ids that sanitise alike stay two files; an already-valid id is returned untouched, pinned by its own assertion after the existing suite caught the first version renaming everything.
boundary: Applies wherever an identifier crosses into a filesystem, URL, network route or shell grammar it was not designed for. Does not apply to ids that are generated to be path-safe by construction.

summary: AI-DE handed agent terminals nine AIDE_* variables and not AGENT_SESSION, which coord-core.py reads. Beyond the session being invisible in .agents, the pre-commit boundary printed an advisory and returned 0 - so the control that stops one session committing over another's files was disabled for every agent launched from the IDE. Observed the same day in a consuming repo: a squash merge swept another session's whole pack refresh into a commit describing only the merger's work, and nothing objected.
tests: AiDe.App.Tests.AgentCarriesThePacksIdentityTests.TheVariablesReachTheEnvironmentATerminalIsLaunchedWith - observed failing with the assignment removed
control: WorkbenchShell.PackSessionId derives a path-safe id from the surface id and the shell sets AGENT_SESSION/AGENT_NAME; tests assert the id survives Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, that distinct panes stay distinct, and that the variable reaches the environment through the shell's own hook rather than by calling the helper twice.
boundary: Applies wherever a launcher composes an environment for a child whose guards degrade to advisory on a missing input. Does not apply where the guard fails closed - there the omission is visible.
